newsitem.title: USA: Progress seen in Crown, Texas union talks.
newsitem.headline: Progress seen in Crown, Texas union talks.

text.p: A union negotiator for locked-out workers at Crown Central Petroleum Corp's Pasadena, Texas refinery said on Wednesday there has been some progress in talks on a new labor pact at the refinery.

"We just submitted a counter-proposal, and they are taking it under advisement," said Joe Campbell, secretary-treasurer with the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Local 4-227. He declined comment on specifics of the latest proposal, made during a bargaining session late Tuesday.
A spokesman at Crown's Baltimore headquarters was not immediately available for comment.

The independent refining and marketing company locked out union workers at its 100,000 barrel per day Pasadena, Texas refinery on February 5 after some equipment was vandalized following expiration of the union's contract.

Talks on a new labor pact have bogged down over the company's demand to replace union workers with contractors and ignore seniority in laying off union employees. The latest round of talks was called by a federal mediator.
"We've told them from Jump Street they could lay off as many as they want, as long as they do it by the terms of the contract, which is seniority," Campbell said.
